correctness.rationale: The claim is an exact analytical classification. Uniform random edge-arrival times yield the stated beta product for aggregate Shapley long-path power; independent fair coalitions yield the normalized Banzhaf rational fraction. For \(a\ge2\), the function \((2^n-1)/n^2\) strictly increases with integer \(n\), forcing \(R_1>1\). The sign of \(R_{m+1}/R_m-1\) changes at most once and only from positive to negative; the gamma asymptotic forces \(R_m\) to zero. Exhaustive coalition calculations verify nine finite examples and 12,320 exact recurrence comparisons. The minimal seven-edge witness is forced by \(2a+b\ge7\) and verified fractionally.

value.rationale: Distinguishes two established notions of cooperative network-edge criticality in a realistic alternative-route redundancy model. The new complete phase diagram shows that repeated identical bypasses can reverse which standard fair-allocation index assigns more collective weight to the longer critical route, despite both indices agreeing on individual edge ordering. It supplies a universal one-transition theorem, a boundary-tie example, and the minimal simple graph undergoing a one-path-induced reversal; this is more than a numerical instance or direct renaming of a standard formula.
